name: get_metrics
description:
checkout-api's service metrics as a table, one row per period, oldest first.

Read this first. Metrics are complete within seconds, while logs can lag by
minutes under load. Columns: requests, error rate, latency p50 and p99, pool
wait p99, pool connections in use, concurrent requests, database query time,
and payments-api latency and timeouts.

minutes.description: How far back to look, ending now. At most 90 rows come back.

period_seconds.description: 10, the alarms' period, or 60 for a longer view.

as_of.description: Replays only: the investigation's now, in ISO 8601 with a time zone. Every read ends there. Left out, reads end at the function's own clock, which also caps a later time.

name: get_recent_logs
description:
checkout-api's newest request log lines, whole, oldest first.

Each line is one request: route, status, latency, version, pool fields, and
for a failure its error type and message, and its stack if it has one. Logs
can trail the metrics by minutes under load, so a missing recent line proves
nothing alone.

minutes.description: How far back to search, ending now.

errors_only.description: Only failed requests (the default), or every request.

limit.description: How many of the newest matching lines to return, at most 200.

as_of.description: Replays only: the investigation's now, in ISO 8601 with a time zone. Every read ends there. Left out, reads end at the function's own clock, which also caps a later time.

name: get_deploy_history
description:
checkout-api's deploys and config changes, newest first, up to now.

Each record has its time, kind (deploy or config), version, commit, author,
message, and for a config change the keys with their old and new values.

as_of.description: Replays only: the investigation's now, in ISO 8601 with a time zone. Every read ends there. Left out, reads end at the function's own clock, which also caps a later time.

name: search_runbooks
description:
checkout-api's runbooks that come closest to what you describe.

Describe what you measured in your own words: the alarm, which signals moved
and which stayed flat, which routes fail and how. The 2 closest runbooks come
back in full (Symptoms, What this is not, Diagnosis), the rest by name only.
The closest runbook is not always the one that fits.

query.description: What you measured, at most 500 characters.

as_of.description: Replays only: the investigation's now, in ISO 8601 with a time zone. Every read ends there. Left out, reads end at the function's own clock, which also caps a later time.

name: read_repo_file
description:
checkout-api's own source code at a release: one whole file, its lines numbered.

Line numbers are the ones stack frames name: a log line's frame
checkout/app.py:72 is line 72 of checkout/app.py at that line's version.
Only checkout-api's modules under checkout/ can be read.

version.description: A release number, as deploy history and log lines give it.

path.description:
One file, exactly as a stack frame names it (checkout/<module>.py).
Left out, the release's files are listed.

as_of.description: Replays only: the investigation's now, in ISO 8601 with a time zone. Every read ends there. Left out, reads end at the function's own clock, which also caps a later time.
